items.title: Protesters haul a guillotine to city council meeting about a potential AI data center, company rep cornered by protestors — ‘ it no longer felt safe to stay,’ developer escorted out by police
items.description: Some protesters brought a guillotine to public consultation for a potential data center in Salem, Oregon. Even though this was displayed outside the venue, it was a confrontation between the data center's representatives and some of the community members that led the latter to leave early.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The Salem City Council convened a public meeting last July 27, where it discussed the proposed $5.1 billion Oakline at Mill Creek data center by Verrus. As the people converged on the meeting site, a TikTok user spotted a guillotine towed by a bike outside of the venue, signaling the people’s discontent with the project. @its.addie.rose ♬ original sound - Addie.Rose According to NewsData, the consultation lasted for more than six hours as several members of the community voiced their opposition towards it. The developer’s representatives were initially on-site to hear the comments, but had to leave midway through as they were confronted by some protesters.“During a break in the proceedings, a group of opposition members cornered Verrus representatives and shouted insulting remarks, to the point where it no longer felt safe to stay,” Verrus spokesperson JP Newmann said, according to the publication. “We appreciate the support of local law enforcement in helping de-escalate the situation and escorting Verrus representatives from the site safely.”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: One week after the meeting, Salem announced a data center moratorium that would halt all data center developments in the city for one year as it considers zoning laws to accommodate developments such as this. This adds Salem to the long list of jurisdictions that have passed similar moratoriums, including Seattle, Washington, and the State of New York.Unfortunately, the Verrus project will likely not be affected by this delay as it filed its application three days before the announcement. Despite this, Governor Tina Kotek (D) announced that Oregon will terminate a deal to sell a 32-acre plot of land that forms part of the three plots of land on which the project will sit. While it still leaves Verrus with approximately 43 acres, it means that it would have to go back to the drawing board to change its plans. This is similar to what Nashville did when it used its eminent domain power to deny the land that another developer wanted to use to build a data center near the historic Nashville Zoo. You may like 142 AI data center protests staged in 42 states as public opposition increases At least 37 people arrested in 2026 so far for protesting against data centers, most for breaking 'petty rules' AI data center developers target rural territory to bypass city construction bans and regulations But because Verrus submitted its application before the moratorium announcement, the city is still processing its proposed data center project. That does not mean that it will get an immediate green light, though. It still has to go through an extensive permitting process, which includes technical studies, permit conditions, and enforceable agreements, among others.Oregon is one of the first states to enact a law that ensures large consumers, like data centers, pay for the majority of the grid upgrades needed to serve their needs. This allowed Portland General Electric, the state’s largest power provider, to increase the bills of users who used more than 20 MW by 30%, while also affecting a 1.3% cut in residential electricity costs. But despite this protection that stops ratepayers from price shocks, many people are still against data center projects in their towns and cities.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
items.author: Jowi Morales
items.titleZh: Protesters haul a guillotine to city council meeting about a potential AI data center, company rep cornered by protestors — ‘ it no longer felt safe to stay,’ developer escorted out by police
items.descriptionZh:
7月27日，美国俄勒冈州塞勒姆市议会召开公众会议，讨论Verrus公司提出的耗资51亿美元的“Oakline at Mill Creek”数据中心项目。会议现场气氛紧张，有TikTok用户拍到一辆自行车拖着一台断头台停在会场外，以此表达对该项目的强烈不满。据NewsData报道，这场听证会持续了六个多小时，多名社区成员发言反对。开发商代表起初在场听取意见，却在中途被迫离场——一群抗议者在休息期间围住Verrus代表，并大声辱骂，场面一度让人感到不安全。Verrus发言人JP·纽曼表示，感谢当地执法部门帮助缓和局势，并安全护送代表离开。

会议一周后，塞勒姆市宣布暂停受理所有数据中心开发申请，为期一年，以便重新审视相关区划法规。这使塞勒姆加入西雅图、纽约州等已实施类似暂停令的司法管辖区行列。但Verrus项目大概率不受此影响，因为其申请在暂停令公布前三天就已提交。尽管如此，俄勒冈州州长蒂娜·科特克宣布，终止出售该项目所在三块地中面积32英亩的地块，这使Verrus手中仍保有约43英亩土地，但不得不重新调整规划方案。此举与纳什维尔市此前用征用权阻止另一开发商在历史悠久的纳什维尔动物园附近建数据中心的先例相似。

由于Verrus在暂停令前提交了申请，市政府仍会继续审批该项目，但并不意味着能快速获批——它仍需经历漫长的许可流程，包括技术研究、许可条件和可执行协议等环节。俄勒冈州是全美最早通过法律，要求数据中心等大用电户为其所需的电网升级承担大部分费用的州之一。该法律允许州内最大电力供应商波特兰通用电气对用电超过20兆瓦的用户加价30%，同时使居民电费削减1.3%。尽管有这一保护机制避免普通纳税人为电价冲击买单，但许多民众依然反对数据中心出现在自己的城镇。这一案例也反映出全美范围内公众对AI数据中心建设抗议增多的趋势——此前已有142起AI数据中心抗议分布在42个州，2026年至今至少37人因抗议数据中心被捕，多数因违反“轻微规则”而遭拘留；部分开发商则转向农村地区以规避城市建筑禁令和监管。

items.title: Anthropic co-designing custom AI inference chips to bypass costly Nvidia GPUs — Samsung reported as manufacturing partner for Claude maker
items.description: Anthropic has announced its building a team to co-design custom ASIC chips for AI inferencing workloads. This will give it greater control over its compute buildout and allow it to make its AI models specifically more efficient for its designs.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Anthropic has announced it's building an in-house chip development team to co-design its own custom ASIC processors for handling AI inferencing workloads. As described to Business Insider, Anthropic is starting to hire engineers to design the chips with an unspecified partner, and it looks set to do it at pace, with the job listing saying that any potential hiree would need to be ready to work to a schedule and get the chip design over the line.This is just the latest major AI company to announce it's developing its own custom hardware. As the global economic shortages squeeze chip supply and models increasingly lean on optimizations to make workloads more efficient and potentially profitable, making custom silicon for your own data centers makes a lot of sense. Anthropic now joins the likes of Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, and OpenAI in building their own chips for the job.If you want something done right...It's no secret that if you want to train an advanced AI model, you need Nvidia GPUs. Even Chinese AI developers, who have the ruling party leaning on them and limited access to Nvidia hardware, still use Nvidia GPUs — even if they have to smuggle them first.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: But if you're looking to run AI to perform inferencing workloads for agentic and generative AI models, you can use a much wider array of hardware. Nvidia GPUs are good, but they're expensive — custom silicon can have a lower total cost of ownership of up to 65% — and power-hungry, and there are much more efficient options available. Chinese labs are using domestic Chinese hardware, and many Western AI developers have their own solutions; those that don't are making them.Google has been building its Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) chips for 12 years, working with Broadcom to develop each generation. Amazon has its Trainium and Inferentia chips, and Meta recently announced several new MTIA designs for deployment through 2027. Microsoft has its Maia line, and Tesla recently pivoted to its AI5 and AI6 chip designs after years of developing Dojo. You may like The custom AI ASIC state of play (May 2026) — Broadcom deals, Google TPUs, Meta MTIA & beyond Broadcom and OpenAI unveil custom-built Jalapeño inference processor Musk's Colossus 1 AI supercomputer's inefficient mixed-architecture design couldn't be used to train Grok, so Anthropic's using it for inference instead And now Anthropic is getting in on the act, and for much the same reasons. Anthropic told Business Insider that it was co-designing the chips so that they would allow Claude to run faster and more efficiently at the scale its customers need. Indeed, Anthropic has seen explosive growth in the past year, seeing huge expansion in the consumer space and taking on significant government contracts — not to mention agentic AI requiring far more tokens than traditional single-prompt interactions.Anthropic hasn't revealed which firm it's working with on the design and development. Although Broadcom and Marvell are the two largest companies in the ASIC co-design market, representing some 95% of it, The Information reported last month that Anthropic was in talks with Samsung for manufacturing.The shovel sellers always benefitDesigning, packaging, and manufacturing your own custom ASIC for AI inferencing isn't cheap, and it isn't easy. Alongside developing the hardware, you need the software stack to utilize it, and you want models that are optimized to run on it to make the most of its potential advantages. That makes it more worthwhile for most companies to simply use other firms' hardware and more general-purpose GPUs. But for major AI companies with enough money to burn and the ability to scale up to maximize efficiency gains, it's well worth the investment.But the AI developers aren't the only ones who benefit. Nvidia has been one of the few companies to make enormous profits from the AI boom, while the likes of Meta, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI are all losing enormous sums of money on their AI efforts. There are very real winners from the custom ASIC design and build market, too: TSMC, Broadcom, and Marvell.Broadcom has been Google's co-design partner for years, and was also recently tapped to help build OpenAI's inferencing chips. It also works with Meta on its MTIA design, as well as holding contracts for other custom ASIC designs with ByteDance and Fujitsu. It also produces strong interconnect and networking hardware, which allows it to offer customers a more complete solution. It claims to have a $73 billion backlog of orders to work through, and expects to generate over $100 billion in annual AI chip revenue by the end of 2027. What to read next Anthropic warns Claude AI is building itself faster than expected, calls for option to halt frontier development Anthropic files to go public AI is starting to out-design chip engineers in narrow areas as LLMs accelerate software chip design tool development Marvell holds massive contracts with Amazon for its Trainium chips and Microsoft for Maia, and is expected to make upwards of $11 billion for these co-design jobs in 2026.If Samsung ends up as Anthropic's partner, it would be a relatively small player in this particular space, but it would bring enormous manufacturing and chip design expertise to the table, as well as access to the all-important memory that is in such short global supply.The biggest winner of all these initiatives, though, is arguably TSMC. The Taiwanese company produces the majority of the world's cutting-edge silicon and is involved in the production of almost all the chips discussed here. They need TSMC's CoWoS advanced packaging technologies for integration with HBM. It also handles much of the packaging of Nvidia's and AMD GPUs, as well as producing much of the underlying wafers.Multi-polar chip worldAnthropic joining the custom ASIC race is hardly surprising and further cements the future we seem to be barrelling towards, which is each of the hyperscaler AI companies looking to handle as much of their inferencing with custom hardware as possible. It's more efficient, easier to control for features and specifications, and easier to scale up when optimized for internal models. From a Chinese perspective, it's also easier to avoid problems caused by international trade blockades and tariffs.They'll likely never become 100% reliant on their own chips — there is just too much AI demand to scale into for that to happen, and Nvidia has been ruthlessly dominating access to the supply chain. But every new chip installed is an Nvidia GPU that won't be used for the same purpose, which may help reduce the stranglehold Nvidia has on the industry. Not for training, though. That's likely to remain Nvidia's biggest appeal for some time to come.
items.author: Jon Martindale
items.titleZh: Anthropic联合设计定制AI推理芯片以绕过昂贵的英
items.descriptionZh:
Anthropic公司近日宣布，将组建内部芯片开发团队，与合作伙伴共同设计定制ASIC处理器，专门用于AI推理工作负载。据Business Insider报道，Anthropic已开始招聘芯片设计工程师，并计划加速推进项目，招聘信息中明确要求应聘者需能够按紧凑时间表完成芯片设计并确保顺利流片。

这一举措并非孤立事件——随着全球芯片供应紧张、AI模型规模持续膨胀，定制芯片正成为各大科技巨头的共同选择。Anthropic并非首家走上这条路的企业：Google与博通合作开发自研TPU芯片已有12年历史，亚马逊拥有Trainium和Inferentia系列，Meta最近公布了多个MTIA设计并计划部署至2027年，微软有Maia系列，OpenAI与博通携手开发了Jalapeño推理芯片，特斯拉在多年研发Dojo之后也转向了AI5和AI6芯片设计。如今，Anthropic正式加入这一行列，标志着AI行业正在整体从“通用GPU”向“专用硅片”迁移。

从技术原理角度看，Anthropic表示，自研芯片将针对Claude模型进行协同设计，使其在客户所需规模下运行得更快、更高效。相比用于训练，AI推理场景的硬件选择要宽泛得多：Nvidia GPU性能强大，但价格昂贵、功耗高，而定制ASIC在总拥有成本（TCO）上可降低高达65%，且在特定模型负载下拥有更高的能效比。这一点对Anthropic尤为关键——过去一年里，其消费者业务爆炸式增长，还承接了大量政府合同，尤其是Agentic AI（智能体AI）需要比传统单轮交互多出数个数量级的token，算力需求呈指数级上升。因此，专门的推理芯片能够在成本、延迟和能效上实现更优的平衡。

不过，芯片设计只是冰山一角。除了硬件本身，厂商还需要配套软件栈和针对模型优化的编译器，才能完全释放定制硬件的潜力。这意味着只有资金充裕、能规模化分摊成本的大型AI公司才有能力自研芯片，其他企业则更倾向于使用现成的通用GPU。

Anthropic尚未透露其芯片设计合作伙伴，但ASIC协同设计市场由博通和Marvell主导，两家合计约占95%市场份额。据The Information上月报道，Anthropic正在与三星洽谈代工制造事宜。三星在该领域虽然算较小玩家，但拥有强大的制造与芯片设计能力，尤其在当前全球内存短缺的环境下，三星在存储芯片（HBM）方面的优势将成为关键竞争力。

值得关注的是，AI芯片自研浪潮的最大受益者并非AI公司本身，而是背后的“卖铲人”——台积电（TSMC）、博通和Marvell。博通长期以来是Google TPU的协同设计伙伴，最近又参与OpenAI推理芯片项目，还为Meta MTIA、字节跳动和富士通提供定制ASIC设计服务。博通拥有包括互联和网络硬件在内的完整解决方案，目前订单积压额高达730亿美元，预计到2027年底AI芯片年收入将超过1000亿美元。Marvell则握有亚马逊Trainium和微软Maia的大规模合同，预计2026年仅协同设计收入就将超过110亿美元。而最大的赢家当属台积电——全球绝大多数先进硅片由其代工，几乎所有上述芯片的生产都需要用到台积电的CoWoS先进封装技术来集成HBM，它同时也负责Nvidia和AMD GPU的大部分封装和底层晶圆制造。

这场芯片格局的演变正在走向一个“多极化的芯片世界”。对Anthropic而言，加入定制ASIC竞赛非常合理，这也进一步巩固了一个明显的趋势：每一家超大规模AI公司都在尽可能用自研硬件来处理推理负载。自研芯片在效率、功能可控性、以及针对自家模型优化后的可扩展性方面都具显著优势；对于中国厂商而言，还能有效绕开国际贸易封锁和关税壁垒。当然，这些公司短期内不可能100%依赖自研芯片——AI需求的增长远超芯片供应，Nvidia仍牢牢掌控着供应链。但每安装一片新自研芯片，就意味着一块Nvidia GPU不会用于同一用途，这有助于削弱Nvidia在行业中的垄断地位。不过，在AI训练领域，Nvidia GPU在可预见的未来仍将保持无可撼动的核心地位。

7月27日，美国俄勒冈州塞勒姆市议会召开公众会议，讨论Verrus公司提出的耗资51亿美元的“Oakline at Mill Creek”数据中心项目。会议现场气氛紧张，有TikTok用户拍到一辆自行车拖着一台断头台停在会场外，以此表达对该项目的强烈不满。据NewsData报道，这场听证会持续了六个多小时，多名社区成员发言反对。开发商代表起初在场听取意见，却在中途被迫离场——一群抗议者在休息期间围住Verrus代表，并大声辱骂，场面一度让人感到不安全。Verrus发言人JP·纽曼表示，感谢当地执法部门帮助缓和局势，并安全护送代表离开。

由于Verrus在暂停令前提交了申请，市政府仍会继续审批该项目，但并不意味着能快速获批——它仍需经历漫长的许可流程，包括技术研究、许可条件和可执行协议等环节。俄勒冈州是全美最早通过法律，要求数据中心等大用电户为其所需的电网升级承担大部分费用的州之一。该法律允许州内最大电力供应商波特兰通用电气对用电超过20兆瓦的用户加价30%，同时使居民电费削减1.3%。尽管有这一保护机制避免普通纳税人为电价冲击买单，但许多民众依然反对数据中心出现在自己的城镇。这一案例也反映出全美范围内公众对AI数据中心建设抗议增多的趋势——此前已有142起AI数据中心抗议分布在42个州，2026年至今至少37人因抗议数据中心被捕，多数因违反“轻微规则”而遭拘留；部分开发商则转向农村地区以规避城市建筑禁令和监管。

history.title: Anthropic co-designing custom AI inference chips to bypass costly Nvidia GPUs — Samsung reported as manufacturing partner for Claude maker
history.description: Anthropic has announced its building a team to co-design custom ASIC chips for AI inferencing workloads. This will give it greater control over its compute buildout and allow it to make its AI models specifically more efficient for its designs.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Anthropic has announced it's building an in-house chip development team to co-design its own custom ASIC processors for handling AI inferencing workloads. As described to Business Insider, Anthropic is starting to hire engineers to design the chips with an unspecified partner, and it looks set to do it at pace, with the job listing saying that any potential hiree would need to be ready to work to a schedule and get the chip design over the line.This is just the latest major AI company to announce it's developing its own custom hardware. As the global economic shortages squeeze chip supply and models increasingly lean on optimizations to make workloads more efficient and potentially profitable, making custom silicon for your own data centers makes a lot of sense. Anthropic now joins the likes of Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, and OpenAI in building their own chips for the job.If you want something done right...It's no secret that if you want to train an advanced AI model, you need Nvidia GPUs. Even Chinese AI developers, who have the ruling party leaning on them and limited access to Nvidia hardware, still use Nvidia GPUs — even if they have to smuggle them first.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: But if you're looking to run AI to perform inferencing workloads for agentic and generative AI models, you can use a much wider array of hardware. Nvidia GPUs are good, but they're expensive — custom silicon can have a lower total cost of ownership of up to 65% — and power-hungry, and there are much more efficient options available. Chinese labs are using domestic Chinese hardware, and many Western AI developers have their own solutions; those that don't are making them.Google has been building its Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) chips for 12 years, working with Broadcom to develop each generation. Amazon has its Trainium and Inferentia chips, and Meta recently announced several new MTIA designs for deployment through 2027. Microsoft has its Maia line, and Tesla recently pivoted to its AI5 and AI6 chip designs after years of developing Dojo. You may like The custom AI ASIC state of play (May 2026) — Broadcom deals, Google TPUs, Meta MTIA & beyond Broadcom and OpenAI unveil custom-built Jalapeño inference processor Musk's Colossus 1 AI supercomputer's inefficient mixed-architecture design couldn't be used to train Grok, so Anthropic's using it for inference instead And now Anthropic is getting in on the act, and for much the same reasons. Anthropic told Business Insider that it was co-designing the chips so that they would allow Claude to run faster and more efficiently at the scale its customers need. Indeed, Anthropic has seen explosive growth in the past year, seeing huge expansion in the consumer space and taking on significant government contracts — not to mention agentic AI requiring far more tokens than traditional single-prompt interactions.Anthropic hasn't revealed which firm it's working with on the design and development. Although Broadcom and Marvell are the two largest companies in the ASIC co-design market, representing some 95% of it, The Information reported last month that Anthropic was in talks with Samsung for manufacturing.The shovel sellers always benefitDesigning, packaging, and manufacturing your own custom ASIC for AI inferencing isn't cheap, and it isn't easy. Alongside developing the hardware, you need the software stack to utilize it, and you want models that are optimized to run on it to make the most of its potential advantages. That makes it more worthwhile for most companies to simply use other firms' hardware and more general-purpose GPUs. But for major AI companies with enough money to burn and the ability to scale up to maximize efficiency gains, it's well worth the investment.But the AI developers aren't the only ones who benefit. Nvidia has been one of the few companies to make enormous profits from the AI boom, while the likes of Meta, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI are all losing enormous sums of money on their AI efforts. There are very real winners from the custom ASIC design and build market, too: TSMC, Broadcom, and Marvell.Broadcom has been Google's co-design partner for years, and was also recently tapped to help build OpenAI's inferencing chips. It also works with Meta on its MTIA design, as well as holding contracts for other custom ASIC designs with ByteDance and Fujitsu. It also produces strong interconnect and networking hardware, which allows it to offer customers a more complete solution. It claims to have a $73 billion backlog of orders to work through, and expects to generate over $100 billion in annual AI chip revenue by the end of 2027. What to read next Anthropic warns Claude AI is building itself faster than expected, calls for option to halt frontier development Anthropic files to go public AI is starting to out-design chip engineers in narrow areas as LLMs accelerate software chip design tool development Marvell holds massive contracts with Amazon for its Trainium chips and Microsoft for Maia, and is expected to make upwards of $11 billion for these co-design jobs in 2026.If Samsung ends up as Anthropic's partner, it would be a relatively small player in this particular space, but it would bring enormous manufacturing and chip design expertise to the table, as well as access to the all-important memory that is in such short global supply.The biggest winner of all these initiatives, though, is arguably TSMC. The Taiwanese company produces the majority of the world's cutting-edge silicon and is involved in the production of almost all the chips discussed here. They need TSMC's CoWoS advanced packaging technologies for integration with HBM. It also handles much of the packaging of Nvidia's and AMD GPUs, as well as producing much of the underlying wafers.Multi-polar chip worldAnthropic joining the custom ASIC race is hardly surprising and further cements the future we seem to be barrelling towards, which is each of the hyperscaler AI companies looking to handle as much of their inferencing with custom hardware as possible. It's more efficient, easier to control for features and specifications, and easier to scale up when optimized for internal models. From a Chinese perspective, it's also easier to avoid problems caused by international trade blockades and tariffs.They'll likely never become 100% reliant on their own chips — there is just too much AI demand to scale into for that to happen, and Nvidia has been ruthlessly dominating access to the supply chain. But every new chip installed is an Nvidia GPU that won't be used for the same purpose, which may help reduce the stranglehold Nvidia has on the industry. Not for training, though. That's likely to remain Nvidia's biggest appeal for some time to come.

history.titleZh: Anthropic联合设计定制AI推理芯片以绕过昂贵的英
history.descriptionZh:
Anthropic公司近日宣布，将组建内部芯片开发团队，与合作伙伴共同设计定制ASIC处理器，专门用于AI推理工作负载。据Business Insider报道，Anthropic已开始招聘芯片设计工程师，并计划加速推进项目，招聘信息中明确要求应聘者需能够按紧凑时间表完成芯片设计并确保顺利流片。

这一举措并非孤立事件——随着全球芯片供应紧张、AI模型规模持续膨胀，定制芯片正成为各大科技巨头的共同选择。Anthropic并非首家走上这条路的企业：Google与博通合作开发自研TPU芯片已有12年历史，亚马逊拥有Trainium和Inferentia系列，Meta最近公布了多个MTIA设计并计划部署至2027年，微软有Maia系列，OpenAI与博通携手开发了Jalapeño推理芯片，特斯拉在多年研发Dojo之后也转向了AI5和AI6芯片设计。如今，Anthropic正式加入这一行列，标志着AI行业正在整体从“通用GPU”向“专用硅片”迁移。

从技术原理角度看，Anthropic表示，自研芯片将针对Claude模型进行协同设计，使其在客户所需规模下运行得更快、更高效。相比用于训练，AI推理场景的硬件选择要宽泛得多：Nvidia GPU性能强大，但价格昂贵、功耗高，而定制ASIC在总拥有成本（TCO）上可降低高达65%，且在特定模型负载下拥有更高的能效比。这一点对Anthropic尤为关键——过去一年里，其消费者业务爆炸式增长，还承接了大量政府合同，尤其是Agentic AI（智能体AI）需要比传统单轮交互多出数个数量级的token，算力需求呈指数级上升。因此，专门的推理芯片能够在成本、延迟和能效上实现更优的平衡。

不过，芯片设计只是冰山一角。除了硬件本身，厂商还需要配套软件栈和针对模型优化的编译器，才能完全释放定制硬件的潜力。这意味着只有资金充裕、能规模化分摊成本的大型AI公司才有能力自研芯片，其他企业则更倾向于使用现成的通用GPU。

Anthropic尚未透露其芯片设计合作伙伴，但ASIC协同设计市场由博通和Marvell主导，两家合计约占95%市场份额。据The Information上月报道，Anthropic正在与三星洽谈代工制造事宜。三星在该领域虽然算较小玩家，但拥有强大的制造与芯片设计能力，尤其在当前全球内存短缺的环境下，三星在存储芯片（HBM）方面的优势将成为关键竞争力。

值得关注的是，AI芯片自研浪潮的最大受益者并非AI公司本身，而是背后的“卖铲人”——台积电（TSMC）、博通和Marvell。博通长期以来是Google TPU的协同设计伙伴，最近又参与OpenAI推理芯片项目，还为Meta MTIA、字节跳动和富士通提供定制ASIC设计服务。博通拥有包括互联和网络硬件在内的完整解决方案，目前订单积压额高达730亿美元，预计到2027年底AI芯片年收入将超过1000亿美元。Marvell则握有亚马逊Trainium和微软Maia的大规模合同，预计2026年仅协同设计收入就将超过110亿美元。而最大的赢家当属台积电——全球绝大多数先进硅片由其代工，几乎所有上述芯片的生产都需要用到台积电的CoWoS先进封装技术来集成HBM，它同时也负责Nvidia和AMD GPU的大部分封装和底层晶圆制造。

这场芯片格局的演变正在走向一个“多极化的芯片世界”。对Anthropic而言，加入定制ASIC竞赛非常合理，这也进一步巩固了一个明显的趋势：每一家超大规模AI公司都在尽可能用自研硬件来处理推理负载。自研芯片在效率、功能可控性、以及针对自家模型优化后的可扩展性方面都具显著优势；对于中国厂商而言，还能有效绕开国际贸易封锁和关税壁垒。当然，这些公司短期内不可能100%依赖自研芯片——AI需求的增长远超芯片供应，Nvidia仍牢牢掌控着供应链。但每安装一片新自研芯片，就意味着一块Nvidia GPU不会用于同一用途，这有助于削弱Nvidia在行业中的垄断地位。不过，在AI训练领域，Nvidia GPU在可预见的未来仍将保持无可撼动的核心地位。
